PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT

This Purchase and Sale Agreement (this "Agreement") is made as of October 6, 2026 between Harbor Point Realty Trust, a Maryland real estate investment trust ("Seller"), and Ridgeline Industrial Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Buyer").

1. Property.

Seller agrees to sell, and Buyer agrees to purchase, the real property commonly known as 2100 Foundry Lane, Waterbury, Connecticut, more particularly described on Exhibit A, together with the improvements, all appurtenant easements and rights, Seller's interest as landlord under the Leases listed on Exhibit B, the Service Contracts Buyer elects to assume, and all transferable permits, warranties, and intangible property relating to the property (collectively, the "Property").

2. Purchase Price; Deposit.

The purchase price is Twenty-Two Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars ($22,400,000). Within three (3) business days after the Effective Date, Buyer shall deposit One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) (the "Deposit") with Coastline Title Insurance Company, as escrow agent. The Deposit is applicable to the purchase price at Closing, refundable to Buyer only as expressly provided in this Agreement, and otherwise non-refundable after the Due Diligence Period expires.

3. Due Diligence Period.

Buyer has until 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the forty-fifth (45th) day after the Effective Date (the "Due Diligence Period") to inspect the Property and to review the Due Diligence Materials. Buyer may terminate this Agreement for any reason or no reason by written notice given before the Due Diligence Period expires, in which case the Deposit is returned to Buyer and neither party has further obligation except those that expressly survive. Buyer shall restore any damage caused by its inspections and shall indemnify Seller against claims arising from its entry, excluding claims arising from the mere discovery of a pre-existing condition or from Seller's negligence.

4. Due Diligence Materials.

Within five (5) business days after the Effective Date, Seller shall deliver to Buyer the Leases and all amendments, the rent roll, operating statements for the prior three years, the Service Contracts, existing surveys and environmental reports, notices of violation received in the prior two years, and copies of real estate tax bills.

5. Title and Survey.

Buyer shall obtain a title commitment and an ALTA survey. Buyer shall give Seller notice of any objection to title or survey no later than ten (10) business days before the Due Diligence Period expires. Seller may, but is not obligated to, cure any objection, except that Seller shall discharge at or before Closing any mortgage, mechanic's lien, or judgment lien that secures a liquidated amount (a "Monetary Encumbrance"). If Seller does not cure an objection, Buyer may terminate and receive the Deposit or accept title subject to the uncured objection.

6. Representations and Warranties of Seller.

Seller represents that: (a) Seller is duly organized and has authority to enter into this Agreement; (b) the rent roll is accurate in all material respects as of its date; (c) the Leases delivered are true and complete and, to Seller's knowledge, no tenant is in monetary default beyond any applicable cure period; (d) Seller has received no written notice of any pending condemnation or of any uncured violation of law; (e) there is no litigation pending or, to Seller's knowledge, threatened, that would materially affect the Property; and (f) Seller is not a "foreign person" within the meaning of Section 1445 of the Internal Revenue Code. Seller's representations survive Closing for nine (9) months, and Seller's aggregate liability for their breach shall not exceed Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($500,000), with no liability until claims exceed Fifty Thousand Dollars ($50,000).

7. As-Is Sale.

Except for the representations expressly made in Section 6, Buyer acquires the Property AS IS, WHERE IS, AND WITH ALL FAULTS, and Seller makes no other representation or warranty, express or implied, including as to physical condition, environmental condition, zoning, or fitness for a particular purpose. Buyer acknowledges that it has had the opportunity to conduct its own investigation and is relying on it. This Section survives Closing.

8. Operations Pending Closing.

Between the Effective Date and Closing, Seller shall operate the Property in the ordinary course, shall maintain existing insurance, and shall not enter into, amend, or terminate any Lease or Service Contract that would bind Buyer after Closing without Buyer's consent, which may not be unreasonably withheld before the Due Diligence Period expires and may be withheld in Buyer's sole discretion afterward.

9. Closing.

Closing occurs thirty (30) days after the Due Diligence Period expires, through escrow. At Closing, Seller shall deliver a special warranty deed, a bill of sale, an assignment of leases and security deposits, an assignment of contracts, a FIRPTA certificate, an owner's affidavit sufficient for the title company to delete the standard exceptions, and a certificate that its representations remain true. Buyer shall deliver the balance of the purchase price and counterpart assignments.

10. Prorations and Closing Costs.

Rents, real estate taxes, operating expenses, and utilities are prorated as of the Closing date, with delinquent rents collected after Closing applied first to current amounts. Security deposits are credited to Buyer. Seller pays the state and municipal conveyance taxes and the cost of curing a Monetary Encumbrance. Buyer pays the recording fees, the title premium, the survey, and its own diligence costs. Each party pays its own attorneys' fees. Prorations are final ninety (90) days after Closing except for real estate taxes, which are reprorated when the actual bill issues.

11. Casualty and Condemnation.

If before Closing the Property suffers a casualty costing more than $1,000,000 to repair, or a taking of more than five percent (5%) of the land or of any material access, Buyer may terminate and receive the Deposit. Otherwise, the transaction proceeds and Seller assigns the insurance proceeds or award to Buyer, with a credit for any deductible.

12. Default.

If Buyer defaults, Seller's sole and exclusive remedy is to terminate and retain the Deposit as liquidated damages, the parties agreeing that actual damages would be difficult to determine and that the Deposit is a reasonable estimate. If Seller defaults, Buyer may terminate and receive the Deposit together with its documented third-party costs up to One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($150,000), or may seek specific performance, provided Buyer files suit within sixty (60) days.

13. Brokers.

Each party represents that it has dealt with no broker other than Coastline Commercial Advisors, whose commission Seller shall pay under a separate agreement, and each shall indemnify the other against claims by any other broker claiming through it. This Section survives Closing.

14. Notices.

Notices must be in writing and are effective on personal delivery, on confirmed email transmission before 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on a business day, or one business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier, addressed as set out on Exhibit C.

15. Miscellaneous.

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Connecticut. Any action arising out of it shall be brought exclusively in the Superior Court for the Judicial District of Waterbury, Connecticut. Time is of the essence. This Agreement is the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all prior understandings, and may be amended only by a writing signed by both parties. It may be executed in counterparts, and electronic signatures have the same effect as originals. Buyer may assign this Agreement to an affiliate on notice to Seller without releasing Buyer.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.
